key_insight: Biomedical reranking improved how often the right clinical note chunk appeared near the top of the retrieved evidence set, but answer accuracy improved only modestly.
clinical_relevance: For longitudinal clinical note question answering, better evidence ranking may help LLMs find patient-specific facts in long, repetitive records, yet retrieval gains alone do not guarantee substantially better answers.
method: Built a retrieval-augmented QA pipeline for longitudinal notes
Combined PubMedBERT dense retrieval, BM25 lexical retrieval, weighted reciprocal-rank fusion, and MedCPT cross-encoder reranking
Tested on 1,000 open- and closed-ended QA pairs from 200 bariatric surgery patients
evidence_signal: Reranking increased Hit@10 from 46.6% to 60.6% and mean reciprocal rank from 0.2371 to 0.3252, while judge-assessed answer correctness rose from 44.8% to 48.6%.
watch_item: Because retrieval improvements translated only partially into better answers, deployment should account for context-window limits, note duplication, and the gap between evidence selection and generation quality.
paper_title: Evaluating Biomedical Reranking for LLM-Based Question Answering over Longitudinal Clinical Notes
